title: Iron Rusting: Oxygen & Water Requirement
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that simulates an interactive iron rusting chemistry lab experiment demonstrating that rust (iron oxide) forms ONLY when both oxygen AND water are simultaneously present.

## Scene Setup
- Dark lab background (color #1a1a2e). Camera at position (0, 3, 7) looking at origin.
- Ambient light (intensity 0.3) plus a directional light from (5, 8, 5) with intensity 0.8 and a point light near the iron sample (warm tone).
- A lab bench surface: a flat box (8 x 0.2 x 4) at y=0, dark gray metallic material.
- An iron sample: a box (1.2 x 0.8 x 1.2) centered on the bench at (0, 0.5, 0). Initially shiny gray metallic color (#8a8a8a) with metalness 0.8 and roughness 0.3.
- Two labeled glass containers on the bench:
  - Water container: a semi-transparent blue cylinder at (-2.5, 0.6, 0) with a label.
  - Oxygen container: a semi-transparent white/light-gray cylinder at (2.5, 0.6, 0) with a label.

## Environment Controls (DOM Buttons)
- Create a HUD panel (top-right, semi-transparent dark background, rounded corners) with:
  - A toggle button with id='btn-water' labeled 'Water: OFF'. Clicking toggles water presence. When ON, button turns blue (#4488ff) and text reads 'Water: ON'.
  - A toggle button with id='btn-oxygen' labeled 'Oxygen: OFF'. Clicking toggles oxygen presence. When ON, button turns green (#44cc66) and text reads 'Oxygen: ON'.
  - A 'Reset Experiment' button with id='btn-reset' that resets the iron sample to pristine state and turns off both water and oxygen.
  - A readout div with id='rust-percentage' showing 'Rust: 0.0%'.
  - A readout div with id='elapsed-time' showing 'Time: 0.0s'.

## Rusting Physics & Chemistry Logic
- Rust forms ONLY when BOTH water AND oxygen are enabled simultaneously. If only one or neither is active, rust progress must NOT increase (it stays at its current level, does not decrease).
- When both are active, rust percentage increases at a rate of 5% per second, clamping at 100%.
- The iron sample color must interpolate from pristine gray (#8a8a8a) to rust orange-brown (#8B4513) based on rust percentage (0-100). Use linear interpolation on the RGB channels.
- The iron sample roughness must increase from 0.3 to 0.95 as rust goes from 0% to 100%. Metalness decreases from 0.8 to 0.15.
- When rusting is actively occurring (both enabled, rust < 100%), spawn rust-colored particles (small spheres, color #b5651d, radius 0.03) that float upward from the iron surface. Spawn approximately 3 particles per frame. Each particle lives for 1.5 seconds, drifting upward (y += 0.02/frame) with slight random x/z drift, and fades out (opacity 0 at end of life). Remove dead particles from the scene.
- When water is ON, show a subtle blue mist effect: a few semi-transparent blue particles slowly orbiting the iron sample.
- When oxygen is ON, show small white particles gently floating around the iron sample.

## Interaction
- Clicking directly on the iron sample (raycasting) should display a popup div with id='info-popup' showing current material properties: rust%, roughness, metalness. Clicking again or clicking elsewhere hides it.
- Keyboard 'w' toggles water (same as button). Keyboard 'o' toggles oxygen (same as button). Keyboard 'r' resets (same as reset button).
- OrbitControls for camera rotation (import from CDN).

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
- waterEnabled: boolean
- oxygenEnabled: boolean
- rustPercentage: number (0-100, one decimal precision)
- ironColor: {r, g, b} current color of iron material (0-1 float range)
- ironRoughness: number
- ironMetalness: number
- activeParticleCount: number (total live rust + mist + oxygen particles)
- rustParticleCount: number (only rust-colored particles currently alive)
- waterParticleCount: number (blue mist particles)
- oxygenParticleCount: number (white oxygen particles)
- isRusting: boolean (true only when both water and oxygen are on AND rust < 100)
- elapsedRustingTime: number (seconds that rusting has been actively occurring, cumulative)
- experimentResetCount: number (how many times reset was pressed)
- infoPopupVisible: boolean

Ensure the animation loop uses a proper delta-time clock (THREE.Clock) for frame-rate-independent rusting.
physics_constraints: Rust formation requires simultaneous presence of water (H2O) and oxygen (O2). Rate: 5% per second when both present. Rust percentage is monotonically non-decreasing (never decreases except on reset). Color interpolation is linear from gray #8a8a8a to brown #8B4513. Roughness: 0.3 + 0.65 * (rust/100). Metalness: 0.8 - 0.65 * (rust/100). Particles must be cleaned up when lifetime expires. Reset restores all values to initial state.
